official.deadline_note: Bachelor's applicants to the Vejle programmes have a separate admission deadline of 15 March (12:00 noon) for the same September intake; there is no separate scholarship deadline - the admission deadline is the scholarship deadline.
official.application_cycle: September 2027 intake; the DANS portal opens for fee-paying applicants on 1 January 2027 and the master's window closes 1 February 2027
official.status_note: SDU's scholarship page is live and presents the Danish Government Scholarship as an ongoing programme; the next round is the September 2027 intake, with the fee-paying application window opening 1 January 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship is granted as a full tuition fee waiver and will cover the tuition fee for two years (MSc programmes) or three years (BSc programmes). Note that fee waiver covers 30 ECTS per semester. If the number of courses exceed 30 ECTS they are not covered by the fee waiver.
benefits: Full tuition fee waiver for the standard length of the programme - two years for MSc programmes, three years for BSc programmes

The waiver covers the published tuition fee of EUR 17,300 per year for these Faculty of Engineering programmes (SDU tuition rates applying from the September 2026 intake), i.e. EUR 34,600 over an MSc and EUR 51,900 over a BSc at the published rate
Fee waiver covers 30 ECTS per semester
If you receive a scholarship, you will receive a refund of the application deposit fee after June 15
eligibility: Non-EU/EEA citizen enrolling in one of the listed master's programmes at the campus in Sonderborg or bachelor programmes at the campus in Vejle
Not eligible for the Danish State Grant: 'If you are eligible to receive the Danish State Grant, you cannot be considered for the scholarship.'
Master's applicants: if you have applied for more than one programme at SDU, you will only be considered for the scholarship if the master's programme is your highest priority
Bachelor's applicants: highest score in the online admission test (uniTEST) leads to an interview invitation
requirements: Master's: submit the application for admission no later than February 1 - even if you have a Danish residence permit
Bachelor's: submit the application for admission no later than March 15
Your application must include all necessary documentation at the time of submission (it must not be necessary for SDU to ask for further documentation)
All documents must be uploaded to the online application at the time of application; SDU does not accept any documents sent by email
To keep the scholarship, demonstrate satisfactory academic progress each semester - as a guideline, completing at least 30 ECTS per semester
Master's: upload the application deposit fee receipt (EUR 200 for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens)
documents: Official Bachelor's transcripts and diploma in English, Danish, Swedish or Norwegian - must include grades and ECTS/units/credits for each course
Course descriptions for the courses on the transcripts (verified)
Self-assessment form (Electronics and Mechatronics) for master's applicants
selection_criteria: Master's: the scholarships are awarded to the best-qualified candidates based on the grade point average of the bachelor's degree and an online interview with key persons from the master's programme
Bachelor's: the scholarships are awarded to the best-qualified candidates based on the result in the online admission test (uniTEST) and an online interview with key people from the study programme
Master's interviews take place between February 19 and 27; bachelor's interviews take place in early June
coverage: Full tuition fee waiver for two years (MSc programmes) or three years (BSc programmes), equal to the published tuition fee of EUR 17,300 per year for these programmes
Fee waiver covers 30 ECTS per semester; courses beyond 30 ECTS are not covered
No travel, accommodation or insurance coverage is stated on the official page
application_method: No separate scholarship application is needed - apply for admission to one or more of the relevant programmes through SDU's online application portal DANS
Master's fee-paying applicants pay the EUR 200 application deposit fee before submission and upload the email receipt to the application
official.application_route: Apply for admission through the DANS application portal by 1 February (master's) or 15 March (bachelor's); the admission application itself is the scholarship application - there is no separate scholarship form.
official.citizenship_residency: You must be a non-EU/EEA citizen enrolling in one of the listed programmes; if you are eligible to receive the Danish State Grant (SU), you cannot be considered for the scholarship.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship exists specifically for highly qualified non-EU/EEA citizens, i.e. international fee-paying applicants; EU/EEA and Swiss applicants pay no tuition at SDU and are outside this scheme.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Restricted to seven named programmes: MSc in Engineering - Electronics/Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering and Mechatronics at Sonderborg, and BSc in Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Interactive Technology Engineering and Software Engineering at Vejle.
official.duration: Two years for MSc programmes, three years for BSc programmes
official.description: The Danish government offers a limited number of scholarships through the Danish Government Scholarship programme to highly qualified applicants in recognition of the important investment that overseas students make during their education. SDU grants the award as a full tuition fee waiver to non-EU/EEA citizens enrolling in specific programmes at its Sonderborg and Vejle campuses.
official.program_type: Danish Government Scholarship (full tuition fee waiver)
official.english_requirement: Proof of English language proficiency must be included in the application. SDU accepts IELTS Academic overall band 6.5 with no band below 6.5, TOEFL iBT total 83 (no section below 20 in Reading, Writing and Speaking; 4.5 in Listening), or Cambridge C1 Advanced score 180; the test must be taken within the last 2 years and SDU must be able to verify the result no later than the application deadline.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no scholarship form to fill in: your admission application to one of the seven eligible Sonderborg or Vejle programmes is itself the scholarship application, so the scholarship deadline equals the admission deadline. The award waives the full EUR 17,300 per year tuition fee for the standard length of the degree, but you must still self-fund living costs in Denmark and prove you can before the residence permit is issued. Competition runs on your bachelor's GPA (master's) or uniTEST result (bachelor's) plus a short-notice online interview, so the file you upload in January largely decides the outcome.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Academically strong non-EU/EEA applicants to SDU's engineering programmes in Sonderborg or Vejle who can fund their own living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Pay the EUR 200 application deposit before submitting and upload the receipt - it is refunded after June 15 if you are awarded the scholarship
Collect per-course transcripts and diploma in English, Danish, Swedish or Norwegian plus verified course descriptions before the portal opens on 1 January
Book an English test early: the result must be verifiable by SDU no later than the application deadline and no older than two years
Master's applicants applying to several programmes: rank the eligible Sonderborg MSc as your highest priority or you are not considered for the scholarship
Watch the email account used for DANS: interview invitations arrive on short notice (after 15 February for master's, late May for bachelor's)
common_rejection_risks: Uploading an incomplete application - SDU requires all documentation at submission and will not request missing items afterwards
Applying to any programme outside the seven named ones - the waiver only exists for the Sonderborg MSc and Vejle BSc list
Being eligible for the Danish State Grant (SU), which automatically disqualifies you from the scholarship
Master's applicants who rank another SDU programme above the eligible Sonderborg MSc
Registering for more than 30 ECTS in a semester - the excess is not covered by the waiver
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs (housing, food, transport, health insurance) are not covered and must be self-funded; SDU also notes tuition does not cover exam equipment such as computers, printers or calculators, and unpaid tuition or missed registration can put the residence permit at risk.
document_audit: Course descriptions must be verified by the issuing institution - plain translations or self-written summaries are not accepted
Transcripts and diplomas must be in English, Danish, Swedish or Norwegian; other languages require a certified translation
The self-assessment form applies only to Electronics and Mechatronics master's applicants
Nothing may be sent by email - every document must be inside the DANS upload before the deadline
alerts: The 1 February master's deadline applies even if you hold a Danish residence permit - a permit does not extend it
Tuition is invoiced a full year in advance for the September 2026 intake onward; the waiver covers that annual fee but nothing beyond 30 ECTS per semester
The scholarship is conditional on progress: falling below roughly 30 ECTS per semester can end the waiver for the following semester
Bachelor's applicants get one single interview invitation even if they applied to all four Vejle programmes
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in DANS, pay and upload the deposit receipt plus all documents by 1 February (master's) or 15 March (bachelor's), then wait for the short-notice interview; scholarship decisions follow the admission decision.
